Hi Samiha — great to connect. Quick reply with a sketch and attached savings matrix (savings_matrix.xlsx). Happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through details.

Packaging sketch (first pass):
- Pilot (4–6 weeks): evaluation cluster + 25k credit; free Optimize onboarding (batching + KV cache enablement).
- Ramp (1–3 months): commitment-based credits tied to token bands; rolling quarters to align with usage growth.
- Production (annual): committed tier pricing, optional Dedicated slot for SLOs.

Discounts/credits:
- Pilot credit: 25k (applied to hosted usage) to cover initial quantization testing and cache warm-up.
- Early ramp concession: 10% standard for first 90 days on committed monthly spend above threshold, tiered thereafter.
- Ops credit for migration effort: one-time service credit for cache warm-up.

Quantization guidance (short):
- Llama-family: 4-bit quantization (Q4) typically yields 2.5–3x token cost reduction with limited quality regression for classification/assistant completion tasks; good candidate for non-generation-critical paths.
- TGI-style or other decoder-only large models: 8-bit mixed (Q8 or int8) gives more stable output for high-SNR generation; 4-bit sometimes introduces failure cases on longer sequences.

Batching & KV cache notes:
- Expected savings depend on prefix reuse: with 60% prefix hit rate KV cache can reduce active decoder token work by ~35–45%.
- Batching windows: we recommend adaptive batching to balance 95th-pct latency — typical config yields 15–30% cost savings at <5% latency tail increase.

Attached is the savings_matrix.xlsx with an initial numeric sketch. Marissa will follow up on commercial structure and next steps; I looped her in. I'll schedule a demo/technical sync once you confirm availability.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Hi all — brief tech summary and conservative estimates you can use in the quote. Forwarding key points from our infra tests.

1) Quantization recommendations:
- If quality bar allows: start with Q8 (int8) on the production-critical assistant paths; move non-critical or high-volume endpoints to Q4 (4-bit) as a second phase after A/B evals.
- Expected differences: Q8 ~1.6–2x cost reduction vs fp16; Q4 ~2.7–3.2x but with higher risk of subtle generation artifacts on long-context prompts.

2) KV cache assumptions & savings:
- Cache hit rate model: 40–70% realistic depending on prompt similarity. Use conservative 45% for initial quote.
- With 45% hit rate and mixed Q8/Q4 profile, expect 20–30% net token cost reduction (after accounting for cache overhead and TTL).

3) Batching and latency tradeoffs:
- Adaptive batching with a 20ms max window: typical throughput gains of 18–25% and median latency unchanged; 95th-pct increases by ~8–12ms depending on traffic burstiness.
- If OrionAI requires strict 95th-pct SLO (<120ms), we recommend a hybrid policy that prioritizes interactive routes with tighter windows and moves background/analytics calls to larger batches.

4) Suggested pilot configuration:
- 2-week staged plan: (week 1) enable KV cache on dev traffic + quantization A/B; (week 2) expand to canary traffic and measure 95/99 latency, then tune batching windows.
- Data: we'll provide per-route cost/latency breakouts and a regressions dashboard; recommend a P0 prompt set for quality monitoring.

If helpful I can attach the microbench report (internal) and a sample A/B eval script.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
